input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production (owner's standing ventures brief).
task: Deepen (flagship 14) ifc-quantity-takeoff: the Aalseth wall parts that stayed unpaired in the revision change report (NEXT.md parked item)
integrity_issues: Found and fixed false groups the 2026-11-20 Kegonsa change report had published (wall split into wall + door; wall + beam merged; 11 mixed-class pieces merged into a fireplace trim wall); the eval note and post say so.

doc_friction.issue: The parked item 'wall parts that stay unpaired' lived only in NEXT.md; allocate.py's BUILDABLE line did not name it, so finding it needed reading NEXT.md and the 2026-11-20 eval.

goal: Make the IFC revision change report pair every Revit part with its host and stop pairing unrelated elements
notes: Cause 1: an open faceted shell (0.12 mm vertex gap) dropped its loops, so its box was null; 1,048 of 27,668 elements in 22 public/real models had no box. geom.mjs keeps them as `loose` for extents only (box, plan), never sections. Cause 2: a short wall's layers sum 2.3% under the host; groups whose boxes tile the host's box get 5% (tiledGroupTol). Exposed bug: groups mixed classes; now one class family at a time. Verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' 127/127 pass; seeded faults (no loose in solidPoints, no loose in transformSolid, one family for all, 5% for all) each fail a test; Aalseth all unpaired wall parts paired, other counts unchanged; HHS controls unchanged (architect 1 changed, construction 0); eval/compare-builds.mjs vs main on 22 files: 0 volume and 0 area changes, envelope flag agreement 4,420/5,497 -> 4,459/5,522 (HHS architect -2, noted as next buildable item). run_venture_tests.py and venture-preflight results below.
